newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq to sign oil deals with China, France.
newsitem.headline: Iraq to sign oil deals with China, France.

text.p: Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said in remarks published on Saturday that Iraq would soon sign oil deals with China and France to develop huge oilfields in southern Iraq.
"Contracts will be signed shortly with Chinese and French firms to develop a number of oilfields (in the south)," said Rasheed, who was quoted by Iraqi newspapers.

Chinese state-run companies want to develop the billion-barrel Ahdab field while the French ELF Aquitaine and Total have agreed in principle with Iraq to sign for development respectively of the Majnoon and Nahr Umar fields.

Iraq is under U.N. sanctions imposed for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait. The curbs prevent foreign investment in oil. To alleviate Iraqis' sufferings under the sanctions, the United Nations has allowed Baghdad since December to sell $2 billion of oil over six months to buy urgent needs.

Last month Iraq and Russia signed a deal under which Moscow is expected to develop seven billion to eight billion barrels of reserves in the southern Qurna oilfield. Rasheed said the contract would bring Iraq total revenue of $4 billion a year.

Iraq and Turkey are expected to sign in Baghdad an agreement to set up a gas pipeline between the two countries to sell Iraqi gas to Ankara. The agreement will be signed by Rasheed and visiting Turkish Energy Minister Recai Kutan.
The oil minister said Italian companies were interested in developing al-Nasiriya oilfield in southern Iraq. He said the field's production capacity was put around 300,000 barrels per day (bpd).
Rasheed said Iraqi oil terminals in the Gulf were ready to handle six million bpd. Iraq is currently exporting under the oil deal a total of 500,000 to 600,000 bpd.
